AntiPattern.Bad: `class CheckoutPage { constructor(page) { this.page = page; } } ... test('...', async ({ page }) => { const checkout = new CheckoutPage(page); ... });`
AntiPattern.WhyBad: Page Object instantiated by the test instead of supplied by a fixture (`AX_E2E_FIXTURE_BASED_POM`). Reintroduces the manual setup/teardown problem fixtures solve; no per-test lifecycle isolation; the page object cannot expose its own fixture-managed state (intercepts, storage, helpers).
AntiPattern.Good: Define `test = base.extend({ checkout: async ({ page }, use) => use(new CheckoutPage(page)) })`; the test declares `checkout` as an argument and receives a fresh per-test instance.
